subject: Edge evidence onramp & SIEM/tracing coordination
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Edge evidence onramp & SIEM/tracing coordination

Hi Tariq / Acme security team,

Thanks again for walking the onboarding checklist earlier. Attached is our draft evidence requirements PDF (acme_siem_requirements_v2.pdf) — it shows three possible export patterns for your VPC/on-prem environment:

- Forwarder -> Splunk HEC over mTLS (preferred for near-real-time)
- Enclave SFTP drop (batched, daily)
- Syslog relay via rsyslog to our forwarder (low-change, but higher latency)

Two quick asks before we finalize the runbook:
1) Which export mode do you prefer? If HEC, can you provide ingress IP allowlist ranges and whether you can support client certs (mTLS)?
2) Retention/PII constraints — any fields that must be redacted prior to export?
3) Tracing: do you have an OTLP endpoint inside the VPC, or should we recommend an agent (e.g., OpenTelemetry collector) to proxy traces out?

Kimberly / Marissa — can you review the requirements doc and flag anything unrealistic for an on-prem forwarder (network ports, firewall rules, cert exchange steps)?

Tentative next step: 30-minute sync tomorrow (Nov 4) to align onboarding owners.

Thanks,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Manager, Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme_siem_requirements_v2.pdf (PDF, 12 pages)

From: Tariq Khan <tariq.khan@acme.com>

Cc: acme-security@acme.com
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 10:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Edge evidence onramp & SIEM/tracing coordination

Sofia — thanks for the doc and clear options. We discussed internally and here are the current constraints: 

- Preferred: Splunk HEC over TLS, but we cannot do mTLS for third-party ingestion without a change window. Single-sided TLS (token) is currently acceptable.
- Network: we will need destination IPs and a short list of ports; firewall change window is Nov 10-12.
- PII: payment card numbers must be redacted. We can add a filter on our side to mask patterns, but we'd like guidance on doing that safely to avoid losing tokens used in detection rules.
- Tracing: we run an internal OpenTelemetry collector and can expose OTLP/grpc at otlp.acme.internal:4317 only within the VPC. We cannot route OTLP outbound to external endpoints.

Are you able to support: (a) HEC with token auth (no mTLS) and (b) a pull model for traces where your collector reaches into our VPC via a short-lived reverse proxy?

We can do the Nov 4 sync; Tariq will join along with our infra lead.

Thanks,
Tariq
Tariq Khan
Security Engineering — Acme Retail

Tariq / Sofia — quick technical notes from the serving/runtime side (copied Diego who owns the evidence-forwarder components):

1) Splunk HEC (preferred):
   - We can accept HEC token auth (no mTLS) but token rotation is required every 90 days per enterprise policy.
   - Ingress ports: 443 (HEC over TLS). If you can provide a NAT egress range for our agents to call, that simplifies allowlisting.

2) Rsyslog/syslog relay:
   - Use TCP/TLS on 6514 with certs; rsyslog + omfwd to our forwarder is a low-risk fallback.

3) Trace handling:
   - We cannot reach into otlp.acme.internal directly from hosted infra for security reasons. Two viable patterns:
     a) Customer exposes an internal OTLP + OpenTelemetry collector and we run a lightweight "pull agent" in a temporary reverse-SSH tunnel during onboarding to retrieve a sanitized subset.
     b) Customer runs the collector and pushes OTLP to a short-lived proxy (we provide a small container image) that performs sampling & PII scrub and forwards to our OTLP-ingest.
   - Sampling headers: we honor W3C traceparent and recommend initial 1% tail-sampling for traces used in QA.

4) PII redaction: best practice is to mask at the source (your collector) to avoid leakage. We can provide regex snippets in the attached trace-hook-specs-vpc.txt for common PCI patterns.

5) Evidence packaging / retention:
   - We store inbound logs in a segmented bucket for 90 days by default when in Private mode; longer retention requires an SLA addendum.

I've attached a short trace/hook spec and a minimal playbook for firewall rules. Diego — can your team validate whether a reverse-proxy pull or agent container is easier operationally for Acme?

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: trace-hook-specs-vpc.txt (text, 3KB)

All — quick estimate from operations after a quick check: 

- Reverse-proxy pull: ~2 engineering-days to wire a short-lived tunnel, plus 1 security review. Risks: requires opening a management port on Acme side for the duration.
- Agent container (push model): ~3 engineering-days for a hardened container image + docs. Higher customer ops involvement but lower network exposure from our side.

Recommendation: go agent container (push) for production onboarding, and offer reverse-proxy pull as a migration path during the Nov 10-12 firewall window if Acme prefers not to install containers immediately.

Scheduling: I can support the Nov 4 sync; Diego (ops lead) will join and bring a short runbook draft for the agent container flow.

Best,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Infrastructure Ops Lead, Redwood Inference
